content.text: Since we're likely not going to make another 3-series fedora release, it may be best to write a command line utility to replace this critical functionality or document the best workaround.
We're going to have a small bugfix release, but I don't know what your institutional tolerance for running off a branch in the interim is.

This issue doesn't impact me directly, so there's no concern there.  I reported it more for informational purposes, and commented based on my misunderstanding of the decisions regarding Fedora 3 releases and a desire not to press for a release based on this little issue that could be worked around if became more than an inconvenience for anyone.
I tested this using the following steps:
2 installed fedora using the installer generated during the build
4. visited the describe page (verifying the version and that it ran and created the system objects)
6 replaced the objectStore and datastreamStore directories with those from 3.8.0 that were used to identify the problem
9. verified that export of objects using context=archive produced XML
The other export contexts work, but this one results in a stack trace similar to the following:

comments.body: Since we're likely not going to make another 3-series fedora release, it may be best to write a command line utility to replace this critical functionality or document the best workaround.
We're going to have a small bugfix release, but I don't know what your institutional tolerance for running off a branch in the interim is.

This issue doesn't impact me directly, so there's no concern there. I reported it more for informational purposes, and commented based on my misunderstanding of the decisions regarding Fedora 3 releases and a desire not to press for a release based on this little issue that could be worked around if became more than an inconvenience for anyone.

https://github.com/fcrepo3/fcrepo/blob/master/fcrepo-server/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/server/utilities/StringUtility.java#L100

needs to be:

sb.append(str, offset, Math.min(offset + numChars,inputLength));

I tested this using the following steps:
1 built the branch
2 installed fedora using the installer generated during the build
3. started fedora
4. visited the describe page (verifying the version and that it ran and created the system objects)
5 stopped fedora
6 replaced the objectStore and datastreamStore directories with those from 3.8.0 that were used to identify the problem
7. rebuilt the database (derby) using fedora_rebuild.sh
8. started fedora again
9. verified that export of objects using context=archive produced XML
